text: Which format change is the one no automated check can detect?
choices: Reordering two columns while keeping their names unchanged.
Changing the meaning of an existing field — publication year becoming acquisition year, without a rename.
Adding a new column at the end of a CSV file with a header.
Removing a column that no current reader consults.
explanation: The data parses perfectly and is wrong. Adding is safe with header-driven readers; removing and reordering break loudly enough to be caught. A change of meaning produces plausible values of the right type in the right place, which is why the rule is to add a new field and deprecate the old one rather than repurpose. Section 28.2.3's plausible wrong answer, in a file format.
